clue.text: Medicinal herbs? I'm taking dope!

parts.note: simples are old-fashioned herbal remedies, plants used as medicine
I'm loses its apostrophe to give two letters
someone who is on drugs is taking them

explanation.surface: A herbalist confesses to dosing themself on their own plant remedies.
explanation.walkthrough: SIMPLES are medicinal herbs; 'taking' gives ON, as in being on a drug. Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton from the nursery rhyme, used as a name for any foolish person, which is what a dope is.

clue.text: Another word for terribly nosy New York male

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of nosy are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a word to describe an awfully inquisitive man from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges NOSY into SYNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A word with the same meaning as another is exactly another word for it.

clue.text: Cereal crop I planted in jungle

indicators.note: planted in says one thing is set down inside another, here the letter I going into the tangle

parts.note: a jungle in the figurative sense is a confusing tangle, a maze

explanation.surface: A farmer sows a grain crop in the middle of the jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn, the tall grain grown widely for food and fodder, is a cereal crop.

clue.text: Room inside the Parisian grill

indicators.note: inside places the room within the French article

parts.note: le is the French for the, as a Parisian would say it
an attic is a room under the roof

explanation.surface: A description of a room in a Paris restaurant's grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room' and 'grill' suggest a restaurant; grill is the noun for a criss-cross screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A grill in the sense of a grating of crossed bars is a criss-cross framework.

clue.text: Son is bust, forced to eke out an existence

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: forced suggests something pushed out of shape, so the letters of is bust are reworked

explanation.surface: A son has gone bankrupt and must now scrape by on very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges IS BUST into UBSIST, after S for son.
explanation.definitionFit: To live at a bare minimum level, managing to survive, is to eke out an existence.

clue.text: Parade one month ago

parts.note: March is one of the months of the year
ago and past both mean gone by, in the past

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a parade held a month back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial procession of troops past a saluting point is a military parade.

clue.text: Initially, navvies on street work without a break

indicators.note: Initially takes the first letter of navvies

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Labourers repair a road around the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Navvies are British manual labourers, originally canal and railway diggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonstop continues without any pause, so it runs without a break.

clue.text: One who can make an impression?

definitions.text: One who can make an impression?

parts.words: One who can make an impression?
parts.note: the surface suggests someone influential, but here an impression is a dental mould of the teeth

explanation.surface: A description of someone with charisma who leaves a mark on others.
explanation.walkthrough: An impression is also a mould taken of a patient's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking moulds of teeth is routine work for this tooth doctor.

clue.text: Courier called up about chauffeur's uniform?

indicators.note: about puts the reversed word around the uniform
in a down clue, up says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to be called something is to be named it
livery is the uniform worn by servants such as a chauffeur

explanation.surface: A courier phones about the uniform a chauffeur should wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAMED into DEMAN, which goes 'about' LIVERY. 'called up' looks like phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier is a person who delivers parcels and packages, a delivery worker.

clue.text: Naked truth, primarily, about working title

indicators.note: about wraps those letters round the word for working

parts.note: naked and bare both mean unclothed
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of truth

explanation.surface: A phrase about the naked truth surrounding a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'primarily' picks the T of 'truth'. A baronet holds a title rather than being one, a common crossword liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary rank just below a baron, carrying the style Sir, is a British title.

clue.text: Wrote about game, a fixture between two Thames boroughs

definitions.text: a fixture between two Thames boroughs

indicators.note: about here means rearranged, turning the letters of wrote around

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A writer covers a card game, and a sports fixture between two London boroughs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the anagram signal, not 'concerning'. 'fixture' suggests a match; the landmark spans the Thames between Southwark and Tower Hamlets in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous London crossing is fixed in place, linking boroughs on each bank of the river.

clue.text: Clean adapted weapon

indicators.note: adapted means changed to suit, so the letters of clean are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidied-up weapon has been modified.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by mounted knights is a weapon.

clue.text: Tries his cooking before wife produces casserole

indicators.note: cooking suggests ingredients being mixed up, so tries his is rearranged

explanation.surface: A man tries his hand in the kitchen before his wife makes a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges TRIES HIS into IRISHSTE, 'before' W.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb or mutton slow-cooked with potatoes and onions is a traditional casserole dish.

clue.text: Bloodsucker's anger connected with seductress

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who seduces men
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A blood-drinking creature's rage is linked to a temptress.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'connected with' puts the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The undead creature of folklore that drinks human blood is a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Rude about head of venture strapped for cash

indicators.note: about puts the first word round the letter that follows

parts.note: rude and insolent both mean disrespectful

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of venture

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a business venture that has run out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts INSOLENT round V, the 'head of venture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to pay one's debts means being bankrupt, badly strapped for cash.

clue.text: Portion brought back for each voyageur

indicators.note: brought back says the word for portion is read in reverse

parts.note: a part is a portion
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: A share is returned for each fur-trading traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' makes PART into TRAP. Voyageurs were the Canadian canoe-men of the fur trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The voyageurs carried furs, often caught by trappers, so the word stands for a fur-trade woodsman.

clue.text: Put out again about children

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
issue is a formal word for offspring

explanation.surface: Someone publishes something again on the subject of children.
explanation.definitionFit: To publish a book or record a second time is to put it out again.

clue.text: Visible from fashionable location, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard rather than written

parts.note: fashionable is in, and a location is a site, so together in site

explanation.surface: Someone can be seen at a trendy spot, or so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be seen is within view, which is what visible means.

clue.text: Held up by belt, it, netsuke, shows style

indicators.note: Held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Japanese toggle carving hanging from a belt displays some flair.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'shows style' does not substitute for a verb meaning to give a title; 'style' alone does, so 'shows' only links. A netsuke is a carved Japanese toggle worn at the belt.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to give them a name or title, and to entitle is to give a name too.

clue.text: Trip out entertaining revolutionary baseball player

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece takes the other inside
out means not in proper order, so the letters of trip are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An outing is planned that features a revolutionary baseball star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TRIP into PITR, which is 'entertaining' CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the player who throws the ball to the batter is a member of the fielding side.

clue.text: Agent dividing cut in study

indicators.note: dividing says one piece splits the other by sitting inside it

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
a rep, short for representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: An agent is splitting a cut in his study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' is the container signal. Prep is British school slang for homework, which links preparing with studying.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolwork done to get ready for lessons is called prep, so to study can mean to get ready.

clue.text: Nurse in shelter

definitions.meaning: to nurse a grudge is to hold it and keep it alive
a place of refuge, especially a haven for ships

explanation.surface: A nurse working in a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to keep a feeling in mind and a sheltered haven for boats.

clue.text: Beneath which there may be plonkers?

definitions.text: Beneath which there may be plonkers?

parts.words: Beneath which there may be plonkers?
parts.note: plonker is British slang for a fool; here the plonkers are people kissing under a Christmas sprig

explanation.surface: A jokey question about where fools might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for an idiot; at Christmas couples kiss beneath this plant, perhaps looking silly.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasitic evergreen hung at Christmas is the plant people kiss beneath.

clue.text: Cut up rough, at first, in outhouse

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the outbuilding

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of rough

explanation.surface: Something is chopped crudely in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives R, which goes 'in' SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear or slice into strips is to cut up into small pieces.

clue.text: Celebrity, tense, to begin an argument?

definitions.note: a verb phrase, as in the warning don't you dare start

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A famous person, on edge, picks a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start!' warns someone not to begin a row; the question mark flags this colloquial sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, to kick off a quarrel or complaint is to start, as in don't you start.

clue.text: Disregard gentle fooling around involving Conservative

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the jumble takes in the next letter
fooling around suggests messing about, so the letters of gentle are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ignore some mild horseplay that involves a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fooling around' rearranges GENTLE into NEGLET, 'involving' C.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something, or fail to look after it, is to disregard it.

clue.text: A bishop, unaccompanied, gets seafood

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
unaccompanied means alone

explanation.surface: A bishop dining by himself is served shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: This large edible sea snail, prized for its meat and shell, is eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Precisely how rent is paid?

definitions.meaning: exactly, following instructions in every detail
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord, so rent goes to that person

explanation.surface: A question about the exact way a tenant pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is read as one who lets, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Following instructions in every detail means doing them exactly, with complete precision.
